name: ExpertEx
summary: A unified AI studio: chat across multiple models (GPT-4, Gemini), generate images, video and voice, and reuse prompts. It is multilingual and everything sits in one workspace.
best_for: online stores that need a steady stream of product photos and short video ads and would otherwise pay a studio or a freelancer per shoot -- the e-commerce studio pushes results straight to the live store on Ultra and above
skip_if: you need one hero shoot a year (a photographer is cheaper and better), your products are hard to render convincingly, or you want a free tier to evaluate on -- generating always costs credits
honest_knock: The plan cards and the calculator on the same page do not agree, and the gap is large enough to pick the wrong tier. The Starter card estimates 65 product photos or 10 short video ads from 1,000 credits, each using the full balance on one content type; at the calculator's own rates 1,000 credits buys 40 photos or 4 video ads. The card works out at roughly 15 credits a photo and 100 a video against 25 and 250 in the calculator, and the same gap repeats on every tier, so it is a systematic difference rather than a typo. Ask which rate governs before you buy. The second thing to price is that this is a credit product with no free tier. Prompt Builder is free; generating is not. And the cheap trials ($1, $2, $5) are three days rather than a month -- enough to test output quality, not enough to test a monthly workflow. And the fundamental one: AI product photography is judged on whether the output is publishable without a retoucher. Run your own worst product through the trial -- a reflective bottle, a garment with fine texture -- rather than the kind of thing that looks good in every demo.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month on Monthly and $5.83 per month on Yearly for 1,000 credits (read 25 November 2026)
pricing.notes: Pricing read 25 November 2026 on expertex.ai/pricing. On Monthly, the cards show Starter at $7, Premium at $20, Ultra at $45 and Professional at $149, each per month. On Yearly, the displayed monthly equivalents are $5.83, $16.67, $37.50 and $124.17, respectively, next to crossed-out prices of $10, $30, $75 and $250 and the label “2 months free”. Twelve months at the Yearly rate comes to ten months at the Monthly one (12 x $5.83 = $69.96 against 10 x $7 = $70). The cards and their buttons give no total annual charge. On Monthly, Premium, Ultra and Professional each show a 3-Days Trial at $1 (1,000 credits), $2 (2,000) and $5 (5,000); Starter has no trial. The page's own calculator prices the work at 25 credits per product photo, 250 per short video ad and 2,000 per full reel, and reels require Ultra or above. Credits roll over month to month while the subscription is active and are lost on cancellation; you can top up on demand or upgrade mid-month, with upgrades prorated immediately and downgrades taking effect at the next billing date. Prompt Builder is free to use before subscribing. ExpertEx told us through PartnerStack on 11 September 2026 that the “2 months free” label and the card-versus-calculator gap were both with their website team as a priority; on the November reading the label matches the prices. At the browser readings on 22 August and 10 October 2026 the ladder was $10, $30, $75 and $250 monthly with $7, $20, $45 and $149 on yearly billing, and the trials, credit rates and FAQ answers were the same on both dates. That October reading also found a separate Teams tab. Lite is priced per seat with a minimum of 5 seats: $7 a seat a month for 1,000 credits per seat, $18 for 3,000 and $30 for 5,000. Growth, also with a 5-seat minimum, is $59 a seat a month for 10,000 credits per seat and $115 for 20,000, and adds Reels & Shorts Studio early access and E-commerce Studio for 1 store. Ultimate is shown as $3.000 "/seat/month" for 500K total team credits with "Unlimited seats included", covering up to 10 brands and 10 stores; the page does not reconcile the per-seat label with the unlimited seats. On the Teams tab yearly billing is exactly two months free: $25 against $30, $95.83 against $115 and $2,500 against $3,000.
